name: Secondary Avascular Necrosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No standardized formal criteria; diagnosis based on clinical and imaging findings

criteria.description: Presence of joint pain exacerbated by weight-bearing and limited range of motion
Radiological evidence of bone ischemia and necrosis on MRI or X-ray
History of corticosteroid use, alcohol abuse, or other known secondary causes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical symptoms plus confirmatory imaging findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires exclusion of primary (idiopathic) avascular necrosis and correlation with known secondary causes.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Progressive deep joint pain localized to affected bone
searchTerms: deep joint pain worsening over time

pathognomonic.symptomName: Restricted joint range of motion due to bone collapse
searchTerms: joint movement limited by bone damage
restricted joint motion from bone collapse
stiff joint due to bone breakdown

common.symptomName: Joint stiffness especially after periods of inactivity
Limping or altered gait when lower extremity is involved
searchTerms: altered gait with lower limb involvement

common.symptomName: Tenderness on palpation over affected joint

occasional.symptomName: Muscle atrophy around affected joint due to disuse
searchTerms: muscle wasting near joint from inactivity
loss of muscle bulk due to disuse

rare.symptomName: Pathological fractures at necrotic bone sites

searchTerms: joint inflammation secondary to bone disease

rare.symptomName: Systemic symptoms such as low-grade fever in case of secondary infection

laboratory: Non-specific inflammatory markers may be mildly elevated
No specific laboratory test diagnostic for avascular necrosis
imaging: MRI showing bone marrow edema and subchondral signal changes
X-ray demonstrating sclerosis, cystic changes, and eventual bone collapse
CT scan may show detailed bone architecture disruption
genetic: No specific genetic markers identified for secondary avascular necrosis
other: History of exposure to corticosteroids, alcohol, trauma, or other risk factors

distinguishingFeatures: Similar imaging findings but no associated risk factors
Elevated inflammatory markers and positive joint fluid cultures
Rapid joint destruction with erythema and warmth
Localized bone infection with systemic symptoms

redFlags: Sudden worsening of joint pain with inability to bear weight
Signs of joint infection such as erythema, warmth, and fever
Pathological fracture or rapid joint collapse
references: Moya-Angeler J, et al. Avascular necrosis of the femoral head: pathophysiology and current concepts of treatment. J Bone Joint Surg Am. 2015.
Assouline-Dayan Y, et al. Pathogenesis and natural history of osteonecrosis. Semin Arthritis Rheum. 2002.
